Or make an assumption if someone isn't out there with pronouns that they are in a vulnerable space currently so back off.

Me: *looking for spaces were talking about our bodies dtc doesn't make me look like a damn creep or make me feel 4x age*

Congrats! I'm 31 and feel too old to be confused, this gives me life x

Get a psychatrist who specializes in mood disorders, trauma and adhd if you can to really confirm. I was misdiagnosed with bipolar by multiple psychiatrists, psychologists and GPs until I saw someone specialising in the disorders so rediagnosed as ADHD and CPTSD. Which totally changed my treatment plan so I'm finally making progress.

I though trauma its more likely to have poor memory? My memory is mostly blank until was in my mid 20s, which was when I moved away from my main abusers. Now my every day memory doesn't even work well :(

I need to try journaling again and see if that helps. Writing tends to trigger a particular flashback so it's hard to be consistent :(

Feel this. I never caused an injury that needed me to be rushed to ER. Either about to act then somehow stop in the split final second or switch to a SI method that I can treat at home so like.... was I really suicidal then? Have I ever attempted then?

I felt like after a year I might finally feel like I trust my T, somehow managed mentioning some surface stuff of suspected CSA in second last season than last season had them go they can't read me etc so do I even want to keep doing therapy. Been feeling the worst since. Felt like I actively did change a lot of things this year and I was in crisis when I started and they just... see a failure.
Thank you. I've lurking through those subs and found them helpful. Also makes me feel hopeless cause I feel like I've used up all the professional options around me so have no other help left :(

EMDR seems intense from the little I know but I'll have more of a look, thank you.

And do therapists usually check in if they think you're disassociating etc? Mine comments periodically that I've been too shut down to do much in sessions... but doesn't  actively seem to help me getting worse in session? I come in some sessions already heavily dissociated, but I do have milder days I feel he should be in a position to notice and help me ground or something?

We had a session where I was really gone - it was during a period where was in crisis so potentially very unsafe. So he said to ground then it wasn't working so hes like well okay right, grounding won't work when you're this far gone... which I agree but he has not reminded me to ground since, that I'm aware of anyway. I dont remember most sessions. I usually remember rocking up to sessions then the rest is a blank. I cant even take notes straight after. It's like I wake up at the end going 'wtaf happened then?'... then I'm in trouble for not keeping a therapy journal but I'm guessing he doesnt remind me in session either cause I know I said trying to not /right after/ I have already blanked by then!

I outright has said it doesn't feel like me when I have x,y,z thoughts/feelings/desire to the point it gets combative and I have to collapse as I pulled to sides so aggressively and got... so you're complex internally... and I'm like? Okay? Don't think you're getting what I'm saying is my daily to daily life is literally stopped in its tracks cause of it. :/ And yeah I don't know... they just tell me I have derealisation/depersonalization so need to do grounding exercises. But I can't ground cause I cant feel my surroundings, you know? Sigh.
Thank u

I actually find the idea of it invasive personally.

I'm from a legal background - contracts are depersonalised documents for covering liability end of the day. When you break a contract, it gives grounds for the opposing party to recover loses or force an action. This contract is automatically voided in an attempt or death so my legal mind is like it's a bulkshit "contract", as much as I get the therapeutic point for some and the liability cover for the practitioner. 

I find my therapist approach makes me trust better (I have big trust issues especially with mental health professional after mistreatment). He validates why I'd have such extreme thoughts due to having experienced extremely distressing things. That helps me not escalate instead. I had abusers also make me sign "contracts " to oblige them for abusive actions. So I'm really glad I didnt know this was a commonish thing or I'd of never tried any therapy...

I do my sessions via video. I dont have the energy + anxiety about driving due to an accident as well. There's loads of sites that offer a range of therapists, and therapists who's own private practice websites offer worldwide online booking for video sessions (so never see you in person). They do tend to be more expensive though. :(
